qe: The Government of India Act, 1935, proposed the formation of an 'All India Federation'. Which of the following conditions was a prerequisite for its formation?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935 ने एक 'अखिल भारतीय महासंघ' (All India Federation) के गठन का प्रस्ताव दिया था। इसके गठन के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी शर्त पूर्व-आवश्यक थी?
o: States with an allotment of 52 seats in the Council of States should agree to join, and their population should be 50% of the total population of Indian states
All princely states were mandated to join without exception
The federal legislature had to be composed entirely of elected members
The British Parliament had to dissolve the viceroy's executive council
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act proposed a federation comprising provinces and princely states. However, it was conditional: states holding 52 seats in the Council of States had to join, and they had to represent 50% of the total population of all Indian states. These conditions remained unfulfilled, and the federation never materialized.

qe: Under the 1935 Act, subjects at the federal level were divided into 'Reserved' and 'Transferred'. Which of the following was categorized as a 'Reserved' subject?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत, संघीय स्तर पर विषयों को 'आरक्षित' और 'हस्तांतरित' में विभाजित किया गया था। निम्नलिखित में से किसे 'आरक्षित' विषय के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया था?
o: Foreign affairs and Defence
Education and Health
Local government and Agriculture
Industry and Excise
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the 1935 Act's federal structure, 'Reserved' subjects—such as defence, foreign affairs, tribal areas, and ecclesiastical affairs—were administered by the Governor-General on the advice of executive councillors who were not responsible to the legislature.

qe: The 1935 Act introduced a bicameral legislature at the center. What was the name of the upper house and the lower house respectively?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम ने केंद्र में द्विसदनीय विधायिका की शुरुआत की। ऊपरी सदन और निचले सदन का नाम क्रमशः क्या था?
o: Council of States and Federal Assembly
Senate and House of Representatives
Legislative Council and Assembly
Upper House and Lower Chamber
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act provided for a bicameral federal legislature: the upper house was known as the Council of States (260 members) and the lower house was known as the Federal Assembly (375 members).

qe: Which of the following was a major drawback of the Government of India Act, 1935, highlighted by nationalists?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935 की निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी एक बड़ी कमी थी, जिसे राष्ट्रवादियों ने रेखांकित किया था?
o: It was a rigid constitution with no possibility of internal growth as the amendment power was reserved with the British Parliament
It granted complete independence to India instantly
It abolished the communal electorates system entirely
It gave the legislative assembly absolute control over the entire budget
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act was criticized for being highly rigid, as the power to amend it was reserved for the British Parliament, leaving no scope for Indian leaders to modify it based on evolving national needs.

qe: Who famously described the Government of India Act, 1935, as a 'car, all brakes and no engine'?
qh: किसने 1935 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम को 'एक ऐसी कार, जिसमें ब्रेक तो हैं पर इंजन नहीं' (a car, all brakes and no engine) कहकर वर्णित किया था?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru
Mahatma Gandhi
Subhash Chandra Bose
C.R. Das
e: Detailed Explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru described the 1935 Act as a 'car, all brakes and no engine' to highlight that while the Act provided for extensive administrative machinery, the Governor-General's overriding 'safeguards' and 'special responsibilities' effectively blocked any real power for Indians.

qe: What was the primary aim of the 'Individual Satyagraha' launched by Mahatma Gandhi toward the end of 1940?
qh: 1940 के अंत में महात्मा गांधी द्वारा शुरू किए गए 'व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रह' का प्राथमिक उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To show that nationalist patience was not due to weakness and to express people's non-interest in the war
To seize the armouries in various districts
To permanently abolish the land revenue system in Bihar
To form a parallel government in the princely states
e: Detailed Explanation: Individual Satyagraha was launched to demonstrate that the nationalist movement's restraint was not a sign of weakness. It aimed to express that Indians were not interested in the war and made no distinction between Nazism and British autocracy.

qe: Who was the first person to offer individual satyagraha in 1940?
qh: 1940 में व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रह करने वाले पहले व्यक्ति कौन थे?
o: Vinoba Bhave
Jawaharlal Nehru
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Maulana Azad
e: Detailed Explanation: Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first person chosen by Mahatma Gandhi to offer individual satyagraha, followed by Jawaharlal Nehru as the second.

qe: The 'Delhi Chalo Movement' was associated with which phase of the nationalist struggle?
qh: 'दिल्ली चलो आंदोलन' (Delhi Chalo Movement) राष्ट्रवादी संघर्ष के किस चरण से संबंधित था?
o: Individual Satyagraha
Civil Disobedience Movement
Non-Cooperation Movement
Quit India Movement
e: Detailed Explanation: The Individual Satyagraha involved selected individuals making anti-war declarations and moving toward Delhi to mobilize villagers, which led to it being popularly known as the 'Delhi Chalo Movement'.

qe: Why did Gandhi designate Jawaharlal Nehru as his successor despite their differing temperaments and views on industrialization and religion?
qh: गांधी ने जवाहरलाल नेहरू को अपना उत्तराधिकारी क्यों नामित किया, जबकि औद्योगीकरण और धर्म पर उनके स्वभाव और विचार भिन्न थे?
o: Because Nehru reliably reflected the pluralist, inclusive idea of India that Gandhi stood for
Because Nehru was a close relative of the Gandhi family
Because Nehru was the only leader who supported the return to the ancient caste system
Because Nehru promised to abolish the Indian National Congress upon taking charge
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi believed Nehru was the best person to lead because he was a truly all-India leader, admired by women, trusted by Muslims (as a Hindu), and respected in both North and South India, thus embodying the inclusive vision of the nation.

qe: In March 1942, the British government sent the Cripps Mission to India. Who headed this mission?
qh: मार्च 1942 में, ब्रिटिश सरकार ने क्रिप्स मिशन को भारत भेजा। इस मिशन का नेतृत्व किसने किया था?
o: Stafford Cripps
Lord Wavell
Clement Attlee
Lord Mountbatten
e: Detailed Explanation: Stafford Cripps, a left-wing Labourite and a member of the British War Cabinet, was sent to India in March 1942 to seek Indian support for the war effort in exchange for constitutional proposals.

qe: The Cripps Mission offered India 'Dominion Status' with the right to participate in international bodies. Which condition regarding the 'princely states' made the proposal contentious?
qh: क्रिप्स मिशन ने भारत को अंतर्राष्ट्रीय निकायों में भाग लेने के अधिकार के साथ 'डोमिनियन स्टेटस' की पेशकश की। 'देशी रियासतों' (princely states) के संबंध में किस शर्त ने प्रस्ताव को विवादास्पद बना दिया?
o: Members of the constituent assembly would be partly nominated by the princes
Princes would be forced to abolish their thrones and integrate with democratic provinces
Princes would have to fund the entire British war effort
Princes would be granted an absolute veto over the Viceroy's executive council
e: Detailed Explanation: The Congress objected to the Cripps proposal because it envisioned members of the constituent assembly being partly nominated by the princes, rather than elected by the people of those states.

qe: What controversial provision in the Cripps Mission plan provided a blueprint for the partition of India?
qh: क्रिप्स मिशन योजना में किस विवादास्पद प्रावधान ने भारत के विभाजन का खाका प्रदान किया था?
o: The right of any province not willing to join the Union to have a separate constitution and a separate Union
The mandate that all provinces must immediately adopt a common currency
The power granted to the British government to unilaterally annex any state
The requirement for all provinces to report to a central military authority in London
e: Detailed Explanation: The mission proposed that any province not willing to join the Indian Union could form a separate Union and have a separate constitution. This was viewed by the Congress as a clear blueprint for India's partition.

qe: Why did Mahatma Gandhi describe the Cripps Mission proposals as a 'post-dated cheque'?
qh: महात्मा गांधी ने क्रिप्स मिशन के प्रस्तावों को 'पोस्ट-डेटेड चेक' (post-dated cheque) क्यों कहा?
o: Because the offer for independence was linked to an uncertain future after the war, with no immediate transfer of real power
Because the cheque had no monetary value in the Indian banking system
Because the mission failed to acknowledge the existence of the Congress
Because the date on the documents was already expired
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi called it a 'post-dated cheque' because the British promises were for the future, 'after the war'. There was no immediate transfer of power or real share in defence, making the offer hollow given the urgency of the situation.

qe: Which of the following was a reason for the failure of the Cripps Mission according to the Indian National Congress?
qh: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के अनुसार, क्रिप्स मिशन की विफलता का एक कारण निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा था?
o: The absence of any plan for an immediate transfer of power and lack of a real share in defence
The mission insisted on the immediate integration of all princely states
The mission demanded the surrender of the Congress Working Committee
The mission's refusal to recognize the dominion status offer
e: Detailed Explanation: The Congress was deeply disappointed because the Cripps proposals offered no immediate transfer of power, and the Governor-General retained supreme control over the defence of India, reducing Indian leaders to 'liveried camp followers'.

qe: Who stated the following: 'I have not become His Majesty’s first Minister to preside over the liquidation of the British Empire'?
qh: यह किसने कहा था: 'मैं महामहिम का पहला मंत्री इसलिए नहीं बना हूँ कि ब्रिटिश साम्राज्य के विघटन की अध्यक्षता करूँ'?
o: Winston Churchill
Stafford Cripps
Ramsay MacDonald
Clement Attlee
e: Detailed Explanation: This statement was made by Winston Churchill, the British Prime Minister during the Second World War. It reflected his firm opposition to any significant transfer of power or autonomy to India during his tenure.

qe: Which section of Indian society was notably excluded from the franchise under the 1919 Act but saw increased importance in later reforms?
qh: भारतीय समाज का कौन सा वर्ग 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत मताधिकार से विशेष रूप से बाहर रखा गया था, लेकिन बाद के सुधारों में उसका महत्व बढ़ गया?
o: Women
Zamindars
Business class
Princes
e: Detailed Explanation: While the 1919 Act was limited, it did provide the right to vote to women for the first time in India, although it remained restricted by property and education qualifications.

qe: The 1935 Act introduced provincial autonomy. What happened to the 'dyarchy' system at the provincial level?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम ने प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता (provincial autonomy) की शुरुआत की। प्रांतीय स्तर पर 'द्वैध शासन' (dyarchy) प्रणाली का क्या हुआ?
o: It was abolished and replaced by provincial autonomy
It was expanded to include even more reserved subjects
It was made mandatory for all princely states to adopt
It was transferred to the central legislative assembly
e: Detailed Explanation: One of the key features of the 1935 Act was that it abolished the 'dyarchy' system at the provincial level and granted provinces autonomy and a separate legal identity, allowing provincial governments to function with more independence.

qe: The central legislature created by the 1935 Act for the proposed All India Federation would have had how many members in the Council of States?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम द्वारा प्रस्तावित अखिल भारतीय महासंघ के लिए बनाई गई केंद्रीय विधायिका में राज्य परिषद (Council of States) के कितने सदस्य होने थे?
e: Detailed Explanation: The Council of States was designed to be a 260-member house, while the Federal Assembly (lower house) was to have 375 members, with representation distributed between British Indian provinces and princely states.

qe: In the context of the 1935 Act, what does 'residuary powers' refer to?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के संदर्भ में, 'अवशिष्ट शक्तियों' (residuary powers) का क्या अर्थ है?
o: Powers not explicitly assigned to either the federal or provincial lists, which were vested with the Governor-General
Powers held exclusively by the district judges
Powers of the local municipal councils to levy taxes
Powers held by the British Crown over the Indian treasury
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the 1935 Act, the Governor-General was given 'residuary powers'. This meant that any legislative subject not clearly categorized under the federal, provincial, or concurrent lists fell under the Governor-General's authority.

qe: How were the provinces freed from the oversight of the secretary of state and governor-general under the 1935 Act?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत प्रांतों को राज्य सचिव और गवर्नर-जनरल की निगरानी से कैसे मुक्त किया गया?
o: They derived legal authority directly from the British Crown
They were given the power to declare independence
They were allowed to maintain their own independent armies
They could veto any ordinance issued by the central Governor-General
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act granted provinces a separate legal identity. They were no longer under the direct superintendence or direction of the Secretary of State or Governor-General, as their legal authority was henceforth derived directly from the British Crown.

qe: What was the main purpose behind the 'carrot and stick' policy of the British regarding political reforms?
qh: राजनीतिक सुधारों के संबंध में अंग्रेजों की 'गाजर और छड़ी' (carrot and stick) नीति के पीछे मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To isolate the extremists by placating the moderates through concessions, and then suppressing the radicals
To grant immediate and absolute freedom to the Indian population
To build a strong national army managed by the Indian National Congress
To abolish the revenue system and make all lands tax-free for peasants
e: Detailed Explanation: The British 'carrot and stick' approach (repress-placate-suppress) was a strategic effort to divide the nationalist movement. By offering some concessions (carrot) to the Moderates, the British aimed to peel them away from the radical Extremists (stick), making the latter easier to suppress.

qe: During the 1930s, the Congress rule in provinces was a major political development. What was a key limitation for these ministries?
qh: 1930 के दशक के दौरान, प्रांतों में कांग्रेस का शासन एक बड़ा राजनीतिक घटनाक्रम था। इन मंत्रालयों के लिए एक प्रमुख सीमा क्या थी?
o: They had limited control over finances and had to contend with the Governor's special powers
They had absolute power to change the central constitution
They were prohibited from passing any laws related to public education
They were legally forced to implement only the rules prescribed by the Muslim League
e: Detailed Explanation: Although the Congress formed ministries, they operated under the 1935 Act's framework. The Governors retained extensive special powers, and ministers lacked full control over the permanent bureaucracy and finances, often leading to friction.

qe: The 'Lee Commission' (1923) was primarily focused on:
qh: 'ली कमीशन' (1923) का प्राथमिक ध्यान किस पर था?
o: Recruitment and conditions of service for the Superior Civil Services in India
The reform of the agricultural taxation system
The development of a unified national primary education syllabus
The abolition of salt tax in the coastal districts
e: Detailed Explanation: The Lee Commission was appointed to look into the working of the Indian Civil Service and the failure to recruit sufficient British personnel, recommending measures to make service conditions more attractive for Europeans.

qe: Under the 1919 Act, the 'secretary of state for India' was paid out of which treasury for the first time?
qh: 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत, 'भारत के राज्य सचिव' का वेतन पहली बार किस खजाने से दिया गया था?
o: British exchequer
Indian revenue
The Tilak Swaraj Fund
The princely states' royal tribute
e: Detailed Explanation: In an attempt to reduce the 'economic drain', the Government of India Act 1919 mandated that the salary and administrative expenses of the Secretary of State for India should be borne by the British exchequer, not the Indian budget.

qe: Which of the following was a reason for the failure of the 'All India Federation' as proposed by the 1935 Act?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम द्वारा प्रस्तावित 'अखिल भारतीय महासंघ' की विफलता का एक कारण निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा था?
o: The required number of princely states did not agree to join the federation
The Indian National Congress declared a full boycott of the federation
The British Parliament refused to provide any funding
The central legislature could not agree on a common currency
e: Detailed Explanation: The federation required states representing at least 50% of the total population of Indian states to join. Since the conditions for the princes to join were not met, the proposed All India Federation never actually came into existence.

qe: What was the main criticism of the 'Communal Award' (1932) by national leaders?
qh: राष्ट्रीय नेताओं द्वारा 'सांप्रदायिक पंचाट' (Communal Award) (1932) की मुख्य आलोचना क्या थी?
o: It sought to divide the Indian nation by granting separate electorates to the depressed classes
It made the Hindu religion the official state religion
It completely abolished the reservation of seats for Muslims
It mandated the immediate payment of a war tax by all citizens
e: Detailed Explanation: The Communal Award extended the policy of separate electorates to the Depressed Classes, which national leaders felt was a deliberate ploy to weaken the nationalist movement by fracturing the Hindu community.

qe: In the 1935 Act, the three lists for legislative power distribution were:
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम में, विधायी शक्ति वितरण के लिए तीन सूचियाँ कौन सी थीं?
o: Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent
Central, State, and District
Executive, Judicial, and Legislative
Official, Non-official, and Special
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act introduced a three-fold division of legislative powers between the center and the provinces: the Federal List, the Provincial List, and the Concurrent List.

qe: Why was the 1935 Act considered 'reactionary' by many Indian nationalists?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम को कई भारतीय राष्ट्रवादियों द्वारा 'प्रतिक्रियावादी' (reactionary) क्यों माना गया था?
o: Because it provided a rigid constitution that reinforced British control and fostered separatist tendencies
Because it gave full independence to the Princely States
Because it legalized the complete, unconditional transfer of all military forces to the Congress
Because it abolished all forms of taxation inside the Indian provinces
e: Detailed Explanation: Nationalists condemned the Act for its 'safeguards' which maintained British control, its rigid nature, and its expansion of communal electorates, which they argued would promote separatism and undermine national unity.

qe: What role did 'Harijan' weekly, started by Gandhi in 1933, play in his social reform movement?
qh: 1933 में गांधी द्वारा शुरू की गई 'हरिजन' साप्ताहिक पत्रिका ने उनके सामाजिक सुधार आंदोलन में क्या भूमिका निभाई?
o: It was used to propagate his views on the removal of untouchability
It served as the official journal of the Communist Party of India
It focused exclusively on reporting the financial profit margins of the British managing agencies
It campaigned for the expansion of British military recruitment in Bihar
e: Detailed Explanation: 'Harijan' was a crucial media tool that allowed Gandhi to communicate his philosophical arguments against untouchability, educate the public on social reform, and gather support for the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

qe: The 'Linlithgow Commission' of 1928 was appointed to investigate which sector's crisis?
qh: 1928 का 'लिनलिथगो आयोग' (Linlithgow Commission) किस क्षेत्र के संकट की जांच के लिए नियुक्त किया गया था?
o: Indian agriculture
Textile manufacturing
Jute export trade
Foreign managing agencies
e: Detailed Explanation: The Linlithgow Commission was established to inquire into the systemic crisis and the declining productivity of Indian agriculture during the British era.

qe: What was the significance of the 'Individual Satyagraha' move in the history of the 1940 national upsurge?
qh: 1940 के राष्ट्रीय उभार के इतिहास में 'व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रह' (Individual Satyagraha) कदम का क्या महत्व था?
o: It allowed the Congress to show the British that the Indian people's patience was not weakness
It mandated the total dissolution of the Congress Working Committee
It legally enabled the Viceroy to appoint a military dictator in every province
It achieved total, absolute independence by the end of 1940
e: Detailed Explanation: By choosing a few selected individuals to protest, Gandhi ensured the nationalist movement remained active without risking mass repression during the war, while simultaneously demonstrating that the nation's patience had limits and that it was fundamentally opposed to the imperialist war.

qe: Who designated Jawaharlal Nehru as his chosen successor despite the preference of many other senior leaders?
qh: अनेक अन्य वरिष्ठ नेताओं की प्राथमिकता के बावजूद किसने जवाहरलाल नेहरू को अपना उत्तराधिकारी नामित किया?
o: Mahatma Gandhi
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
C. Rajagopalachari
Maulana Azad
e: Detailed Explanation: Mahatma Gandhi officially designated Nehru as his successor because, despite their differences, he felt Nehru most reliably represented the pluralist, inclusive, and modern vision of India he envisioned.

qe: The 'Muddiman Commission' was set up in 1924 to look into what specific political issue?
qh: 1924 में 'मडिमन आयोग' (Muddiman Commission) का गठन किस विशिष्ट राजनीतिक मुद्दे की जांच के लिए किया गया था?
o: The deadlock within the diarchic (dyarchy) dispensation
The financial corruption within the salt manufacturing guilds
The territorial mapping of the North-West Frontier Province
The recruitment of native clerks in the Bengal railways
e: Detailed Explanation: The Muddiman Committee was appointed to assess the functioning of the dyarchical system introduced by the 1919 Act and identify why it had led to administrative deadlocks.

qe: What did Gandhi mean when he stated, 'Hinduism dies if untouchability lives'?
qh: गांधी ने जब कहा, 'हिंदू धर्म मर जाता है अगर अस्पृश्यता जीवित रहती है', तो उनका क्या तात्पर्य था?
o: That the practice of untouchability was a moral stain that made the survival of a progressive Hindu religion impossible
That all Hindu temples must be destroyed to save the religion
That the caste system was the only way to promote national unity
That the Vedas had explicitly mandated the practice of untouchability for all believers
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi believed that untouchability was a perversion and a moral failure that contradicted the essence of Hindu spirituality. He felt that unless this stigma was purged, the religion could not survive as a respected or ethical moral system.

qe: Which of the following was a structural achievement of the Indian leadership regarding the civil service after the enactment of the 1935 Act?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के अधिनियमन के बाद सिविल सेवा के संबंध में भारतीय नेतृत्व की एक संरचनात्मक उपलब्धि क्या थी?
o: The Act allowed for a large share in the administration in the interim period
It mandated that all British officers must resign their posts immediately
It forced the British treasury to pay all salaries of the civil servants in London
It established an independent civil service recruitment commission in every village
e: Detailed Explanation: While the 1935 Act and subsequent negotiations allowed for a greater Indian share in the provincial administration, it did not grant true sovereignty, as the bureaucracy remained largely beyond the reach of elected ministers.

qe: What was the main purpose of the 'Consultative Council of Greater India' proposed by the Simon Commission?
qh: साइमन कमीशन द्वारा प्रस्तावित 'ग्रेटर इंडिया की सलाहकार परिषद' (Consultative Council of Greater India) का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To provide a platform for representatives of both British provinces and princely states to discuss federal issues
To draft the final legal constitution for the independent state of Burma
To manage the tax revenue collection of the central legislative assembly only
To permanently ban the entry of any native Indian into the executive council rooms
e: Detailed Explanation: The commission recognized that India would eventually become a federation. As an intermediate step, it proposed a Consultative Council to bridge the administrative differences between the British-governed provinces and the princely states.

qe: What were the '1935 safeguards' and why were they criticized by the nationalists?
qh: 1935 के 'सुरक्षा उपाय' (safeguards) क्या थे और राष्ट्रवादियों द्वारा उनकी आलोचना क्यों की गई?
o: They were overarching executive powers given to the Governor to protect British interests, which acted as brakes on the reforms
They were financial protections for the poor subsistence peasantry
They were the names of new welfare schools opened by the Congress ministries
They were judicial decrees that granted absolute independence to all lower courts
e: Detailed Explanation: The 'safeguards' were special executive powers granted to the Governor and Governor-General to interfere in legislation, block bills, or take over administration. Nationalists argued these were not for India's welfare, but to protect British influence and 'brakes' on the limited reforms offered.

qe: What did the inclusion of 'provincial autonomy' signify in the 1935 Act's administrative vision?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के प्रशासनिक दृष्टिकोण में 'प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता' (provincial autonomy) को शामिल करने का क्या अर्थ था?
o: Provinces were given a separate legal identity and freed from the superintendence of the central government
Provinces were given the absolute right to declare war on neighboring countries
Provinces were legally forced to adopt a uniform military code issued by the Governor-General
Provinces were allowed to print their own independent fiat currency notes
e: Detailed Explanation: Provincial autonomy meant that provinces were no longer under the direct administrative 'superintendence and direction' of the central government. They gained a separate legal existence, and their executive and financial authority was derived directly from the British Crown.

qe: Which of the following describes the nature of the electorate system introduced by the 1935 Act for the provincial legislatures?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा 1935 के अधिनियम द्वारा प्रांतीय विधानसभाओं के लिए शुरू की गई निर्वाचक प्रणाली की प्रकृति का वर्णन करता है?
o: Communal Award based separate electorates were maintained, and the franchise was significantly expanded
The system of separate electorates was entirely replaced by a uniform adult franchise
It allowed only those who owned land worth 50,000 rupees to vote
It mandated that every voter must be a university graduate
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act maintained and entrenched the divisive communal electorates system. However, it also significantly expanded the franchise, notably granting women the right to vote on the same basis as men, though still within restrictive property/tax criteria.

qe: Why did the British administration eventually fail to establish the 'All India Federation' envisioned by the 1935 Act?
qh: ब्रिटिश प्रशासन अंततः 1935 के अधिनियम द्वारा परिकल्पित 'अखिल भारतीय महासंघ' की स्थापना करने में क्यों विफल रहा?
o: The required participation of the princely states was not achieved due to the strict conditions attached to their entry
The Indian National Congress refused to allow the participation of any state in the federation
The local municipal boards refused to pay the required entry fee
The British Parliament in London voted against the funding of the federal headquarters
e: Detailed Explanation: The federation was a conditional provision. It required princes representing 50% of the total state population to join. The princely rulers remained apprehensive about their sovereignty and largely refused to join on the government's terms, causing the federal provision to remain a dead letter.
